title: Decide what a plan code outside the four-tier ladder means
goal: Plan storage is data-driven: tenant_plans is the authority, the console plan editor creates and disables codes, and the compiled-in four-tier table is only the seed plus a fallback for codes the table does not hold. The frontend feature gate is not data-driven. core/entitlements/plans.ts closes the union to four codes, ranks them 0-3, maps every other code to free, and hides lowcode surfaces below a rank. The code already says so: planOptions.ts:4-20 and TenantList.tsx:256-260 both state that an operator-defined code resolves to free, and the tenant dialog renders a warning when the typed code is outside the ladder. So this is a documented limitation, not a silent bug - but the warning never says what it costs, and the operator has no way to grant a custom plan the feature surfaces its quotas imply. This packet decides which way out and implements nothing.
findings: TC-07 (P3): frontend/src/core/entitlements/plans.ts:16-23 closes TenantPlan to four literals, :58-63 hardcodes PLAN_RANK, :70-75 maps any other code to free, and :37-56 hardcodes the feature-to-tier matrix. The backend accepts any code matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,31}$ (tenant_plan_model.go:76,88-91) and the console plan editor creates one (TenantPlanEditor.tsx, POST /system/tenant-ops/plan).

Concrete consequence: create plan trial with enterprise quotas, assign a tenant to it, log in as that tenant's user. context.tenant.plan is trial, normalizeTenantPlan returns free, PlanFeatureGuard hides lowcode.dynamic-module and the generator pages even though the quota row says otherwise. Quota and visible surface disagree, and only one of them is data the operator controls.

The limitation is documented rather than accidental: planOptions.ts:4-20 explains the four-tier ladder and the fallback, TenantList.tsx:256-260 repeats it at the call site, and TenantList.tsx:831-835 shows system.tenant.plan.outsideLadder when the typed code is outside the ladder. What is missing is the consequence (paid surfaces resolve to free) and any way to attach features to a custom plan.
Second drift: TenantPlanMatrix renders the four built-in tiers from PLAN_FEATURES, so a custom plan is invisible on the console page that is supposed to explain what a plan includes.

No test covers the entitlements module: on 2026-10-27 the frontend unit suite ran 34 files / 230 tests green, and none of them import core/entitlements. The rank and fallback rules are therefore unverified by tests as well as undocumented in the contract.
The backend half is not affected: PlanStore reads the table, GetDefaultQuota is the documented fallback, and tenant_plan_store_test.go pins seed idempotence and quota resolution.

in: Write docs/reviews/TENANT_PLAN_LADDER_DECISION_2026-10-27.md with the concrete consequence above and one row per option

Option A (smallest): accept the ladder. Plans outside it are quota-only by design; make that explicit in the outsideLadder warning copy and in contract section 2.4, and stop presenting the four-tier matrix as if it covered every plan. No source logic changes

Option B: make entitlements server-driven. Add a rank (or tier) and a feature set to tenant_plans, return them through the existing plan payload and the session context, and delete PLAN_RANK, PLAN_FEATURES and normalizeTenantPlan from the frontend. This needs a migration, so it lands as a separate packet outside this program

Option C: keep plans as quota definitions only and remove the plan-driven feature gate: delete the rank machinery, PlanFeatureGuard, the lowcode entries on the plan matrix and the AppLayout path gate; those pages then depend only on page and action permissions, which already exist
Record the recommendation, the cost, and which consequence each option leaves standing
Name the follow-up packet id for whichever option is chosen, and state that the chosen option is not part of V1 completeness
out: Implementing any option in this packet
Adding a migration or changing tenant_plans
Changing what a plan's quota numbers mean
Removing permission checks on the lowcode pages under any option

implementationNotes: This is a decision packet: a wave that changes no source file is a valid closeout.

Do not describe the current behaviour as a defect discovered in this review. The code documents it in three places; the review's contribution is that the consequence is not stated to the operator and the feature matrix does not cover custom plans.

Option A and option C both avoid a migration; option B is the only one that keeps custom plans working with feature gating, and the only one that changes the schema, so it cannot land inside this program.
Option C must say plainly that it gives paid lowcode surfaces to every tenant that has the page permission, because that is the product decision being made, not a side effect.

The recommendation should follow the smallest complete change: if plan-based packaging is not a shipped product requirement, C is smaller than B and honest; if it is, B is the only option that survives; if custom plans are simply quota buckets, A costs a copy change and a contract sentence.
Do not propose keeping the four-tier rank in the frontend while allowing custom codes without saying which option that is; that is the current state.
